body:
Hit this exact thing on a fresh self-hosted `2.19.0_local` and your diagnosis is correct - nice write-up.

**Confirming the root cause:** the SPA gate in `apps/main/index.js` only grants access when `window.PLAN_TYPE ∈ {enterprise, professional, trial}`. `PLAN_TYPE` is injected from `pages/login.jsp` (`${requestScope.planType}`) and resolves via the billing service, which a `local_deploy` box doesn't have - so it comes back `""` and you get blocked, even though `window.DASHBOARD_MODE === "LOCAL_DEPLOY"`. The gate never looks at `DASHBOARD_MODE`/`IS_SAAS`.

**Proper fix:** I opened #6112 to make the gate treat `local_deploy` / non-SaaS deployments as never-paywalled (added to the same bypass as whitelisted orgs / signup pages). That routes OSS logins straight to the dashboard.

**Workarounds until it merges** (either one):

1. *No rebuild* - set a valid plan on your org in Mongo, then restart the dashboard so it re-reads it:
   ```js
   // mongosh
   db.getSiblingDB("billing").organizations.updateOne(
     { adminEmail: "<your-admin-email>" },
     { $set: { planType: "enterprise" } }
   )
   ```
   (Depending on your build the backend may still serve `PLAN_TYPE` empty; if so use #2.)

2. *Frontend* - in `pages/login.jsp`, change `window.PLAN_TYPE = '${requestScope.planType}'` to `window.PLAN_TYPE = 'enterprise'` (or apply the #6112 gate change), and redeploy the WAR.

To answer your Q1 directly: yes, the OSS dashboard is meant to be fully usable on `local_deploy` - this is just a gate that forgot to account for it.
